title: Delta-manifests and quarantine pipeline for incremental verified-profile patches
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: full re-publish of a Redwood-verified performance profile (latency/throughput/cost) for a model version is heavyweight: it requires re-running full benchmark suites, replacing pinned manifests, and coordinated rollouts. This slows remediation for small, low-risk updates (e.g., corrected cost normalization, small sequence-length distribution refinements) and increases blast radius for noisy telemetry-driven refreshes.

Goal: introduce a delta-manifest model and a quarantine/verification pipeline that lets small, bounded changes to verified profiles be published as incremental patches (deltas) that carry explicit change vectors, risk metadata, and automated quarantine verification before full catalog replacement or pin rollforward. Delta patches should reduce cycles-to-publish for low-risk fixes while retaining strong traceability and rollback guarantees.
outcome_metrics: median profile publish lead time reduced from X days to <= 8 hours
fraction of profile changes published as delta patches >= 40%
post-publish performance regressions caught in quarantine < 1% of delta publishes
proposal_summary: We will define a compact delta-manifest schema that encodes: changed fields (e.g., cost_normalization, sequence_buckets, kernel_tag), an explicit risk vector (variance, sample_size, telemetry_lift), and a monotonic patch fingerprint. Publish flow: 1) author delta against base pinned profile; 2) run targeted quarantine verification (synthetic microbench + sampled shadow traffic); 3) if quarantine passes, allow staged promotion (catalog side-by-side with base) and optional auto-rollforward after thresholded telemetry. If quarantine fails, auto-reject and open ENG tickets. All deltas are signed and archived in the profile ledger for provenance.
design_decisions: Delta schema will be additive/non-destructive: never mutate base profile in-place without an explicit rollforward action
Quarantine runs must exercise the same runtime kernels and quantization paths as target deployment (avoid synthetic-only verification)
Deltas will carry a numeric risk score; automated promotion rules will gate on risk <= threshold or explicit steward approval
All published deltas are signed with a steward key and recorded in the signature ledger for audit and rollback
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): implement delta-manifest schema and authoring UI; internal-only publishing to alpha catalog
Phase 2 (quarantine): build quarantine harness that runs microbenchmarks + 1% sampled shadow traffic; integrate with CI and runtime test fleet
Phase 3 (promote): allow delta-staged promotion with auto-rollforward policies for low-risk deltas; expose manual steward approval flow for P1/P0 changes
Phase 4 (GA): announce documented contract, update onboarding checklist, instrument console to show delta lineage and risk vectors
acceptance_criteria: Delta-manifest schema v1 implemented and documented
Quarantine harness executes against runtime test fleet and produces pass/fail + variance report
Console shows delta lineage and provides steward approval button
At least 3 distinct low-risk profile fixes published as deltas during alpha with no regression incidents
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: delta semantics accidentally provide incompatible guarantees with older clients -> Mitigation: maintain strict compatibility checks and require a compatibility flag in delta manifest
Risk: noisy telemetry leads to churned delta publishes -> Mitigation: require minimum sample_size and effect size thresholds before auto-promotion
Risk: operational complexity increases -> Mitigation: bundle with steward UX, clear runbooks, and automated remediation playbooks
open_questions: What is the exact numeric formula for the delta risk score? (ENG to propose)
Should deltas be allowed to change pinned model_version references or only metadata/cost/sequence buckets?
What retention window for archived deltas (90 days vs 1 year)?
timeline: Nov 2025: schema definition + prototype authoring CLI
Dec 2025: quarantine harness integration + alpha publishes
dependencies_notes: Depends on ENG kernel-tag mapping in ENG-20222 and performance-catalog API extensions in PM-52345. Quarantine requires test fleet capacity allocation and cost budgeting.
updates: 2025-11-12: Draft created; scoped schema fields and initial acceptance criteria
